name: MLAgentBench
description: A benchmark of 13 machine learning experimentation tasks where agents must read and write files, execute Python code, and iteratively improve ML models. Tasks range from established datasets (CIFAR-10, ogbn-arxiv) to novel Kaggle challenges. The best agent achieves 37.5% average success rate — 100% on well-established tasks but 0% on novel Kaggle challenges never seen in training.
evaluation_method: task success rate (% improvement over baseline performance threshold)
general_score_metric: success rate (% tasks where agent improves over baseline by required threshold)
typical_sota_score: ~37.5% average; 100% on established tasks; 0% on novel Kaggle challenges
reputation: Published at ICML 2024; foundational benchmark for ML research automation; referenced in AI-scientist work (SakanaAI); revealed complete failure on novel Kaggle tasks despite success on established ones
notes: ICML 2024. The stark contrast between 100% success on known datasets and 0% on novel Kaggle challenges reveals that agents are primarily doing pattern matching against training data rather than genuine ML experimentation. Agents operate via file I/O, bash commands, and Python execution. Referenced extensively in subsequent AI-scientist and AI-research-automation papers. Open-source with simulated ML research environments.
